definitions.explanation: A geographical area defined for the purposes of local government administration. In Japan, this typically refers to the wards within designated cities (政令指定都市) or other administrative subdivisions.

examples.japanese: この{市|し}は{七|なな}つの{行政区|ぎょうせいく}に{分|わ}かれている。
examples.english: This city is divided into seven administrative wards.

examples.japanese: {行政区|ぎょうせいく}ごとに{窓口|まどぐち}が{設|もう}けられている。
examples.english: Service counters are set up for each administrative district.

examples.japanese: {横浜市|よこはまし}には{十八|じゅうはち}の{行政区|ぎょうせいく}があり、それぞれに{区役所|くやくしょ}がある。
examples.english: Yokohama has eighteen administrative wards, each with its own ward office.

notes:
Composed of {行政|ぎょうせい} (administration; government) and {区|く} (ward; district). Refers specifically to divisions created for administrative purposes, as opposed to natural or informal regional boundaries.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {行政区|ぎょうせいく}{画|かく}: administrative division/demarcation
- {行政区|ぎょうせいく}{域|いき}: administrative district area
- {行政区|ぎょうせいく}の{再編|さいへん}: reorganization of administrative districts
- {行政区|ぎょうせいく}{分|ぶん}け: division into administrative wards

JAPANESE ADMINISTRATIVE DIVISIONS:
In Japan, {行政区|ぎょうせいく} typically refers to the wards ({区|く}) within {政令指定都市|せいれいしていとし} (designated cities) such as {大阪市|おおさかし}, {横浜市|よこはまし}, and {名古屋市|なごやし}. These are distinct from Tokyo's {特別区|とくべつく} (special wards), which have greater autonomy.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {区|く}: ward — the ward itself, without the administrative connotation
- {選挙区|せんきょく}: electoral district — a district defined for voting purposes
- {自治体|じちたい}: municipality; local government — the governing body itself, not the geographical area
